title: ANARI OS and the AI Agent Ecosystem | Anari Energy
meta: ANARI OS runs charging sites in production. Around it, 18 agents cover acquisition, delivery, operations and growth — each labelled live, pilot or planned.

sections.h1: An operation, not a hardware vendor.
sections.lede: Hardware is the part you can photograph. What keeps a site earning is the layer above it: monitoring, fault triage, maintenance dispatch and the commercial work that follows go-live. Two of those agents are already measurable: N-Tech cut support response from 4 hours to 90 seconds, and N-SDR delivers 5x lead-screening efficiency.
sections.credit: Installed unit in service · cold-climate site, Finland

sections.lede: Most vendor pages describe an agent ecosystem as if all of it were live. This is the honest split: what is in production, what is in pilot, and what is still a plan.

items.title: Monitoring & remote support
items.text: Fleet telemetry, alarm triage and remote intervention. Response measured in seconds rather than hours.

items.title: N-Tech maintenance
items.text: Diagnostics and field dispatch in production since Q4 2025 — support response 4 hours to 90 seconds.

items.title: N-SDR demand generation
items.text: Outbound screening at 5x lead-screening efficiency, supporting acquisition after go-live.

items.title: Design & sizing agents
items.text: Site study and system design assistance — used on live projects, still under human sign-off for final specification.

items.title: Knowledge & training agents
items.text: Operator training and documentation generation, being trialled with new site handovers.

items.title: Autonomous energy trading
items.text: Tariff-arbitrage and demand-response orchestration. Architected, not deployed — we are not claiming it as a feature today.

sections.lede: The agents are grouped by the business function they serve, not by the technology they use. A layer is only useful if the one before it produced something real.

items.title: Acquire
items.text: Market scan, lead screening and commercial analysis before a site is chosen.

items.title: Deliver
items.text: Site study, design assistance and compliance tracking during the build.

items.title: Operate
items.text: Monitoring, fault triage, maintenance dispatch and operator training.

items.title: Grow
items.text: Demand generation and utilisation growth after the site is live.

items.title: Orchestrate
items.text: Cross-agent scheduling with a human approval gate on anything irreversible.

sections.h2: Where a human still signs off
sections.lede: An operations system that can change tariffs, dispatch work orders or trade energy without a human in the loop is a liability. These gates exist on purpose.

items.title: Final equipment specification
items.text: Agents draft; an engineer signs. A wrong rating is expensive and physical.

items.title: Tariff and pricing changes
items.text: Proposed with a rationale and a simulation, applied by the operator.

items.title: Field dispatch
items.text: Diagnosed and scheduled automatically; the site visit still needs a human decision.

items.title: Anything irreversible
items.text: The same rule we apply to our own automation: no silent external action.

sections.h2: See the operations layer against your own site.
sections.lede: If you already operate chargers, the useful comparison is not a feature list — it is fault-to-fix time and what your data currently shows.
